title: Confinement and scarcity: maternal rearing conditions and offspring performance in a predatory mite of biological control relevance
content: Predatory mites in the family Phytoseiidae are among the most widely deployed biological control agents for the control of small arthropod pests such as spider mites, thrips, and whiteflies. To be effective agents, they are commercially mass-produced before they can be released. However, rearing conditions used to mass-produce these predators are not well researched, but to optimize rearing, it would be beneficial to know optimal conditions for aspects such as cage size, prey density, and impacts of rearing generation after generation in enclosed arenas. Gong et al. (2026) ask a simple but consequential question: does it matter how cramped or how well-fed a mother mite is, not just for her, but for her daughters?
